assumedContext: Share count is 597m following the April 2026 capital increase.

findings.claim: FY2026 targets are reaffirmed at EUR 2.4bn of adjusted EBITDA, EUR 0.7bn of adjusted net income after minorities and a dividend of EUR 0.80 per share. H1 2026 delivered EUR 1.24bn of adjusted EBITDA and EUR 0.4bn of adjusted net income, so the full-year target is tracking.
findings.label: MANAGEMENT GUIDANCE

findings.claim: On 597m shares, EUR 0.7bn of adjusted net income is roughly EUR 1.17 per share. At EUR 22.90 that is about 19.5x earnings — which is not a cheap multiple for a utility, and it is a direct consequence of the 62% increase in the share count.
findings.label: ANALYST ESTIMATE

findings.claim: The Kozani data centre is the thesis's most specific claim and the least contracted. Phase I targets 300 MW operational by the end of 2028, with expansion potential to 1 GW. Total Phase I investment is roughly EUR 3.5bn, of which PPC contributes about EUR 1.2bn.
findings.label: FACT
findings.source: PPC April 2026 announcement and Greek press

findings.claim: There is no signed anchor tenant. PPC has been in talks with four hyperscalers — Google, Meta, AWS and Microsoft — toward a joint venture in which the partner takes a long-term land lease and a 10-year power purchase agreement from nearby PPC solar parks. Partner selection was targeted for the end of summer 2026 and no agreement has been announced.
findings.label: FACT
findings.source: Greek financial press reporting on the Kozani process

findings.claim: The structural consequence is decisive. PPC's EUR 1.2bn is roughly a third of the Phase I cost; the partner funds the rest. Without a signed partner the project does not proceed at the announced scale, and PPC's own commitment does not substitute. The 300 MW campus is a plan contingent on a counterparty that does not yet exist.
findings.label: ANALYST ESTIMATE
findings.source: Derived: EUR 1.2bn of a EUR 3.5bn Phase I

findings.claim: The contrast within this batch is exact and instructive. Constellation has signed 920 MW of nuclear PPAs at 18.5-year average duration; Vistra is described as holding hyperscaler PPAs. PPC has a process. Under this protocol's classification test that is the difference between [Existing Contracted] and [Unfunded Planned], and it is the difference between earnings and a press release.
findings.label: ANALYST ESTIMATE
findings.source: Derived; cross-reference to the Constellation dossier

findings.claim: Demand classification: current generation, supply and distribution earnings are [Existing Contracted] and operating; the 7.3 GW renewable fleet is [Existing Contracted]; the funded portion of the 2026-2030 capacity plan is [Approved / Committed Pipeline]; the Kozani 300 MW campus is [Unfunded Planned] pending a partner; and the 1 GW expansion ambition and the EUR 8bn regional data-centre vision are [Speculative Demand] earning zero base-case weight.
findings.label: ANALYST ESTIMATE

findings.claim: The dividend policy and the capital programme are in visible tension. PPC targets EUR 0.80 per share in 2026 rising to EUR 1.40 by 2030. On 597m shares that is roughly EUR 3.3bn of dividends over the plan period — against the EUR 4.5bn just raised from shareholders. The company is returning about three-quarters of its equity raise as dividends while borrowing to build.
findings.label: ANALYST ESTIMATE
findings.source: Derived: average DPS ~EUR 1.10 x 597m x 5 years

risks.text: The Kozani campus has no signed anchor tenant. PPC's EUR 1.2bn is about a third of Phase I cost; without a partner the project does not proceed at the announced scale.
At roughly 19.5x adjusted earnings on the enlarged share count, the equity is not cheap for a utility, whatever the enterprise multiple says.
The dividend policy returns roughly EUR 3.3bn over the plan against the EUR 4.5bn just raised, while the build is funded 31% by new debt.
All guidance is on an adjusted basis during a lignite phase-out, when the gap to statutory earnings can be large.

catalysts.text: Announcement of a Kozani anchor tenant and joint venture structure
FY2026 results against the EUR 2.4bn EBITDA and EUR 0.80 dividend targets

conclusions: Operating delivery is on track: H1 2026 adjusted EBITDA of EUR 1.24bn against a reaffirmed FY2026 target of EUR 2.4bn, with adjusted net income after minorities of EUR 0.7bn and a EUR 0.80 dividend.

But on 597m shares that is roughly EUR 1.17 of adjusted EPS and about 19.5x earnings — not a cheap multiple for a utility, and a direct consequence of the 62% share-count increase the thesis does not mention.

The Kozani data centre is the thesis's most specific claim and its least contracted. Phase I is 300 MW by end-2028 at roughly EUR 3.5bn, of which PPC funds about EUR 1.2bn — and there is no signed anchor tenant, only a process with four hyperscalers.

That is decisive rather than pedantic. PPC's contribution is about a third of the cost; without a partner the project does not proceed at the announced scale. Under this protocol it is [Unfunded Planned] and earns zero base-case weight.
The contrast inside this batch makes the point: Constellation has 920 MW signed at 18.5-year average duration. PPC has a shortlist. That is the difference between earnings and a press release.
thesisImpact: Phase 3 removes the data centre from the base case and puts the equity on its operating earnings, where the enlarged share count makes it look expensive rather than cheap. The dividend is the strongest part of the story and is what will produce most of the return in the base case.
